summary: Short-lived API keys causing intermittent 429 spikes during concurrent uploader sessions
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports sudden 429 throttles observed only when their fleet of short-lived API keys (spawned per-upload session) are used by concurrent uploader workers. Impact: Upload workers see 1–3 minute bursts of 429 responses that stop after keys expire or when request rate drops. This affects ingestion throughput and causes backoff/retry storms in the uploader.

Environment: Dedicated pool (tenant id t-streamline), prod-us-east, multi-host uploader fleet using temporary keys minted by their integration service.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Customer provisions 50 short-lived API keys (TTL 5m) and assigns them round-robin to 200 upload workers.
2) Each worker opens parallel streaming requests (concurrency 8) to the /v1/embeddings route.
3) After ~2–3 minutes, a subset of workers begin receiving 429s clustered in 10–30s windows.
4) When keys expire and new ones are minted, bursts re-occur.

Observed behavior & logs:
- Gateway logs show 429 responses with quota_reason: "token_bucket_exhausted" and bucket_id values that map to a small set of backend counters.
- Quota-service metrics (sample) show sharp drops in available_tokens for some bucket hashes, followed by refill after TTL.
- Edge logs indicate the incoming requests were evenly distributed across hosts; however the quota counters appear concentrated.

Customer expectation: Distribute quota fairly across keys and avoid coordinated bursts tied to key rotation.

Customer notes: They expanded concurrency to scale and noticed the 429s correlated to their key rotation cadence; previously using long-lived keys this did not occur.
comments: 2026-03-10 Priya Nair: Ticket opened after customer escalated to Support via #support. Included request rate graphs and a sample of gateway logs.

2026-03-10 Liam O'Connor: Assigned. Initial hypothesis: per-key bucket affinity + host-local caching of quota counters causing uneven depletion during key fan-out. Requested quota-service bucket debug logs and request hashes.
2026-03-11 Customer (StreamlineAI): Provided exporter logs and a diagram of key minting service. Confirmed short TTL and round-robin assignment.
2026-03-11 SRE (Nina Alvarez): Observed metric spikes in quota-service on node-3 and node-7 around the same windows. Added tracing for bucket hash calculation.
2026-03-12 Liam O'Connor: Added temporary mitigation steps and asked customer to throttle key rotation to 1/10th and report impact.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis A: Short-lived keys produce burst of new bucket allocations; quota-service cache warm-up routes many requests to same bucket_id due to modulo hashing combined with number-of-buckets change.

Hypothesis B: Edge path normalization earlier observed (SUP-246813) was not the root cause; request paths were consistent. Root cause more likely related to per-key token bucket sharding plus host affinity.
Reproduced in internal lab by simulating 60 short-lived keys and 120 parallel workers; observed 429 windows matching customer reports.

Captured quota-service debug dump: bucket_hash = hash(api_key || route || tenant) mod N where N is current bucket shard count. When N changes due to autoscaling or cached-config mismatch, many keys map to same shard unexpectedly.
Observed that dedicated-pool autoscaler triggered a scale-up between bursts; control-plane config propagation lag (30–90s) caused temporary mismatch of N across quota-service instances.
Result: temporary concentration of token accounting on a subset of shards leading to exhaustion and 429s until refill; rotation then repeats the pattern.
resolution:
Short-term workaround provided to customer (2026-03-12):
- Increase API key TTL to reduce churn OR
- Add jitter to key minting so keys do not rotate in tight synchronized windows OR
- Reduce per-key concurrency (recommend concurrency per key <= 4 for current tenant limits)

Support performed configuration change (non-disruptive) to quota-service in prod: enabled cross-instance bucket-consistency mode which forces queries to a central coordination layer for 60s after config changes to avoid N mismatch windows.
Follow-ups: Engineering change scheduled (2026-03-18) to make shard-count propagation synchronous during autoscale events for dedicated pools. Add telemetry alert for bucket-consistency anomalies.
Customer agreed to keep ticket open for 7 days to confirm stability; no data loss or billing impact identified.
